SeriesStatAccessor::movvar¶

Back to SeriesStatAccessor API Reference

Series SeriesStatAccessor::movvar() const
Series SeriesStatAccessor::movvar(std::int64_t window) const
Series SeriesStatAccessor::movvar(std::int64_t window, std::int64_t dim) const

Series SeriesStatProxy::movvar(std::int64_t window, std::int64_t dim) const

What It Does¶

movvar() computes population variance inside every trailing window while preserving shape. The default window is three on the last axis.

Population is important here: each window divides squared deviations by its actual number of values, not by N-1. The first startup window contains one value and therefore always has variance zero.

Parameters And Return Shape¶

window sets the maximum trailing width and must be positive. dim selects the axis carrying order; it defaults to the last axis and accepts negative indexing. Every position receives one variance, so the result preserves shape and has floating dtype.

Examples¶

Example 1. The default three-position window begins with two partial windows.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0});
std::cout << x.stat.movvar() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0.25, 0.66666667, 0.66666667]

Example 2. With width two, every full window contains adjacent values whose population variance is 0.25.

std::cout << x.stat().movvar(2) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25]

For window three, the startup pair [1,2] has mean 1.5 and population variance (0.25+0.25)/2 = 0.25. Full windows [1,2,3] and [2,3,4] both have population variance 2/3.

Gradient¶

Within a window of actual length N, the derivative for member x_i is 2(x_i-window_mean)/N. Reverse mode accumulates that term from every trailing window containing the input. Constant windows send zero sensitivity because all centered deviations are zero.

Example 3. Overlapping windows accumulate their reverse contributions.

auto tracked = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 4.0});
tracked.tracks_slope_(true);
tracked.stat.movvar(2).sum().reverse();
std::cout << tracked.sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.5, -0.5, 1]

The middle value participates in both nontrivial windows: it is above the mean of [1,2] but below the mean of [2,4], so its contributions partially cancel.

Choosing Moving Spread¶

Use movvar() when squared units are useful in later algebra, such as variance addition or volatility objectives. Use movstd() when readers need spread in the original units. Neither method uses the sample estimator.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Partial prefixes use their actual length.

  • There is no unbiased argument.

  • window must be positive; omitted dim selects the last axis.

See Also¶

  • movstd: square root of the same trailing population variance.

  • var: reduce a lane to one variance.
